newsitem.title: JAPAN: Oil stain seen around stricken Russian tanker.
newsitem.headline: Oil stain seen around stricken Russian tanker.

text.p: Japanese authorities rescued 31 crew members of a Russian-registered oil tanker who were found adrift in life boats in rough seas west of Japan on Thursday, Maritime Safety Agency officials said.
One sailor was still missing, however, and coastguard vessels and helicopters were searching the area, officials said.
In Moscow, a Russian emergencies ministry official said the vessel had broken into two but it was unclear whether the tanks were damaged.
"The latest we have is that there is an oil stain 1,800 metres by 100 metres, but neither we nor the Japanese know whether or not there is a major leak," the Russian official said.

"We also do not know whether it is still afloat or not," he added. Japanese officials had said earlier that the tanker was taking on water and listing amid high waves. Fog in the area was reported to be severely limiting visibility.

The sailors had earlier abandoned the 13,157-ton Nakhodka some 100 km (60 miles) northeast of the Oki Islands in the Sea of Japan, about 700 km (420 miles) west of Tokyo, the Japanese agency officials said.

There were conflicting rewports of the size of her cargo. Japan's Kyodo news agency said the vessel was carrying an estimated 1,900 tonnes of crude oil from China to Russia but Russian emergencies ministry officials insisted it was loaded with 19,000 tonnes of crude.
